title: Prediction, Self-Fulfilling Prophecy, and Predestination Paradox Separation Pattern
purpose: Separate three related but distinct concepts: prediction, self-fulfilling prophecy, and predestination paradox. Prevent false collapse between ordinary forecasting, belief-driven outcome creation, and closed causal time-loop structures.

core_definition.summary: A prediction is a forecast about what may happen. A self-fulfilling prophecy is a forecast or belief that changes behavior in a way that helps produce the forecasted outcome. A predestination paradox is a closed causal time loop where an event causes actions in the past that make that same event happen.
core_definition.governing_rule: Do not treat every prediction as causation, every belief as destiny, or every causal loop as a normal forecast.

core_separation.corrected_equation: prediction = forecast; self_fulfilling_prophecy = forecast_or_belief + behavior_change + outcome_reinforcement; predestination_paradox = closed_time_loop + event_causes_its_own_causal_conditions
core_separation.one_line_translation: A prediction guesses the outcome; a self-fulfilling prophecy helps make the outcome happen; a predestination paradox loops the outcome back into its own cause.

prediction.definition: A prediction is a forecast, estimate, or claim about what may happen in the future.
prediction.key_feature: The prediction does not have to cause or influence the outcome.
prediction.plain_example: Someone says, 'I think it will rain tomorrow.' The statement does not cause the rain.
prediction.boundary: A prediction is not proof, causation, destiny, or automatic outcome control.

self_fulfilling_prophecy.definition: A self-fulfilling prophecy is a belief or prediction that influences behavior in a way that helps make the predicted outcome happen.
self_fulfilling_prophecy.key_feature: The belief affects conduct, and conduct helps produce the result.
self_fulfilling_prophecy.plain_example: Someone believes they will fail a test, stops studying, panics, and then fails.
self_fulfilling_prophecy.boundary: The prophecy is not magic or destiny; it works through behavior, choices, social reaction, pressure, avoidance, or expectation effects.

predestination_paradox.definition: A predestination paradox is a closed time-travel causal loop where an event is caused by actions that only happen because of that same event.
predestination_paradox.key_feature: The cause and effect form a loop with no clear original starting point.
predestination_paradox.plain_example: A person travels back in time to prevent a disaster, but their actions accidentally cause the disaster they tried to prevent.
predestination_paradox.boundary: A predestination paradox is not just a strong prediction; it requires closed-loop causality, usually through time travel or fictional time mechanics.

comparison_table.mechanism: Estimate based on evidence, pattern, intuition, or reasoning.
comparison_table.example: I think it will rain tomorrow.

comparison_table.core_meaning: Belief or forecast that helps make itself true.
comparison_table.mechanism: Belief changes behavior; behavior changes outcome.
comparison_table.example: I think I will fail, so I stop studying, then fail.

comparison_table.core_meaning: Closed causal loop where the outcome helps cause itself.
comparison_table.mechanism: Future event causes past action; past action causes future event.
comparison_table.example: A time traveler tries to prevent a disaster but causes it.

targeted_false_collapses.collapse: A prediction automatically causes the outcome.
targeted_false_collapses.correction: A prediction can be passive. It only becomes causally relevant if it changes behavior, decisions, or conditions.

targeted_false_collapses.collapse: A self-fulfilling prophecy is the same as destiny.
targeted_false_collapses.correction: A self-fulfilling prophecy usually works through behavior and expectation, not unavoidable fate.

targeted_false_collapses.collapse: A predestination paradox is just a prediction that came true.
targeted_false_collapses.correction: A predestination paradox requires a closed causal loop where the future and past create each other.

targeted_false_collapses.collapse: Believing something makes it automatically real.
targeted_false_collapses.correction: Belief only affects reality through action, interpretation, social feedback, avoidance, pressure, or other causal mechanisms.

targeted_false_collapses.collapse: Trying to prevent an event always proves predestination.
targeted_false_collapses.correction: Prevention attempts only become predestination paradoxes if the attempt is already part of the event's causal loop.

D1_deduction.question: What must be true for each concept?
result: Self-fulfilling prophecy requires forecast or belief plus behavior/outcome influence.

A1_abduction.question: What could explain an outcome matching a prior statement?
result: The prediction was accurate but passive.
The prediction changed behavior and became self-fulfilling.
In a fictional time-loop context, the event may be a predestination paradox.
The match may also be coincidence, pattern recognition, or post-hoc interpretation.

R_reduction.question: What does the evidence actually prove?
result: A forecast coming true proves accuracy, not causation by itself.
Behavior change after the belief supports self-fulfilling prophecy analysis.
A closed time-loop structure is required before predestination paradox applies.

A2_reconstruction.question: After removing inflated meaning, which classification remains?
result: If there is only a forecast, classify as prediction.
If the forecast changed behavior and produced the result, classify as self-fulfilling prophecy.
If future and past cause each other in a loop, classify as predestination paradox.

D2_deduction.question: What final distinction must hold?
D2_deduction.result: Prediction is not automatically causal. Self-fulfilling prophecy is causal through behavior. Predestination paradox is causal through a closed time loop.

distortion_tests.name: Forecast Test
distortion_tests.question: Is this simply a claim about what may happen?

distortion_tests.name: Behavior Change Test
distortion_tests.question: Did the belief or prediction change what someone did?

distortion_tests.name: Outcome Reinforcement Test
distortion_tests.question: Did that changed behavior help produce or confirm the outcome?

distortion_tests.name: Closed Loop Test
distortion_tests.question: Does the outcome cause the past condition that causes the outcome?

distortion_tests.name: First Cause Test
distortion_tests.question: Is there a clear origin, or is the cause trapped inside a loop?

distortion_tests.name: Proof Boundary Test
distortion_tests.question: Is someone treating a guess, belief, or loop story as proof beyond what the evidence supports?

classification_flow.compact_flow: claim detected -> forecast checked -> behavior influence checked -> time-loop checked -> classification assigned

steps.question: Is there a statement about an outcome?
Is the statement predicting what may happen?
Did the prediction change behavior or conditions?
Did the changed behavior help produce the predicted outcome?
Is there closed-loop causality between future and past?
Is this prediction, self-fulfilling prophecy, predestination paradox, coincidence, or insufficient evidence?

failure_modes.name: Prediction Inflation
failure_modes.description: Treating an accurate forecast as if it caused the event.

failure_modes.name: Belief-as-Magic Error
failure_modes.description: Treating belief as if it directly changes reality without action or mechanism.

failure_modes.name: Feedback Loop Blindness
failure_modes.description: Missing how expectation changed behavior and helped create the result.

failure_modes.name: Time-Loop Overreach
failure_modes.description: Calling something a predestination paradox when there is no actual closed causal loop.

failure_modes.name: Post-Hoc Destiny Rewrite
failure_modes.description: Looking backward after an event and pretending the result was always inevitable.

psc_lock.prediction: A prediction says what might happen.
psc_lock.self_fulfilling_prophecy: A self-fulfilling prophecy helps make itself happen through behavior or feedback.
psc_lock.predestination_paradox: A predestination paradox is a closed causal loop where trying to change the event is already part of causing it.
psc_lock.one_line_translation: Guessing, causing through expectation, and looping through time are three different structures.

taglines: A self-fulfilling prophecy changes the play.
A predestination paradox completes the loop.
A belief is not destiny unless behavior or structure makes it causal.
You did not change the timeline; in a predestination paradox, you completed it.
